text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-INC-9472 fired for service="inference-request-queue"
incident-bot: metrics: queue_length=6123, inflight=980, drop_rate=2.4% (> threshold 1%), avg_wait=28s
incident-bot: severity=P1 — paging #eng-oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/queue-backlog

pagerduty: Page acknowledged by alice (oncall) — incident assigned to alice

alice: ack — I'm on it. First glance: spikes across all regions or just us? Any deploys in last 15m?

bob: Noticed a spike in HPA reconcile latency earlier. Autoscaler-controller logs show repeated 429s to cloud provider API around 22:14 UTC. Reconcile lag > 90s which explains it not scaling fast enough.

bob: quick metrics dump:
```
metrics.inference_autoscaler.reconcile_latency_p95 = 142.3s
metric.request_queue.length = 6123
cluster.api.429_rate = 0.32
```

carol: I can jump in but wrapping a CSM call in 15m. @bob if you can take lead please, I'll stay available for escalation.

bob: taking lead. Plan: 1) manual scale to relieve immediate backlog 2) check controller logs for 429 root cause 3) if provider throttling, route traffic to dedicated pool as fallback.

bob: manual scale command I'm running now:
```
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/inference-backend --replicas=45
kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/inference-backend
```

incident-bot: Manual scaling event detected: inference-backend replicas 25 -> 45 by bob at 22:19:03 UTC

alice: seeing partial tail drain. queue_length dropping 6123 -> 2100 within 3m. tail latency down from 2.6s -> 1.1s for steady requests. Dropped requests still visible but trending down.

dave: FYI CS: three customers reported 503s during 22:12-22:21 UTC. One customer on Dedicated had degraded throughput. Notifying them and opening support tickets.

bob: digging into autoscaler-controller logs: provider returned 429s due to burst rate limit. A temporary mitigation: increase controller's retry/backoff and stagger scale requests. We'll request quota increase but that will take time. Also applying shorter cooldown and more aggressive scale target for now.

carol: applied temporary policy change: raised minReplicas from 10 -> 20 for the inference namespace via feature-flag to reduce future spurts. Command:
```
api patch hpa inference-backend -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 20}}'
```

alice: routing note: we also enabled fallback routing to dedicated-pool for heavy workloads to protect shared capacity. Observability shows dedicated pool capacity absorbing ~1.1k qps now.

bob: monitoring: drop_rate reduced from 2.4% -> 0.1%, queue_length stabilizing ~350-500. Still watching for controller to recover.

dave: CS updated affected customers; one asked for postmortem once we have root cause.

carol: handing over to @erin (next oncall) in 20m. Handoff summary: manual scale applied (25->45), minReplicas bumped to 20, fallback routing enabled, provider API returned 429s — likely rate limits. Action items: follow up with provider for quota, tune autoscaler backoff, add circuit-breaker for long-tail requests, verify postmortem.

erin: acknowledged handoff. I'll watch through the night and start postmortem draft tomorrow. If replica count stabilizes, we can gradually revert the aggressive minReplicas after 6h of stable metrics.

alice: keeping PD open for now; closing once stable for 30m and customers acknowledged. Great work team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-INC-9472 note: manual actions recorded, incident state=investigating -> mitigated (monitoring).
